verdict.line: You lose if you brawl into his E (Footwork) shield and W (Path Maker) stun before he's spent them; you win if you catch him with E (Footwork) down and chain Q (Broken Wings) into W (Ki Burst) before he can reset.

brief.thesis: K'Sante holds lane and solo-kill advantage here because his E (Footwork) shield (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s cooldown) absorbs exactly the burst window Riven's all-in is built around, and his Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks into a shockwave pull that punishes your dash-ins at close range. Riven's Q (Broken Wings) cooldown doesn't shorten with rank (fixed 13s), so her trade frequency is capped while his W/E/Q get cheaper every level — she has to win the cooldown-timing game, not the raw-stat game. The data backs this up: 48.5% win rate across 724 games, defensive shape.

theirWindow.when: He holds 2 Q stacks and E (Footwork) up
theirWindow.what: Do not walk into melee range — the Q (Ntofo Strikes) shockwave pulls you in and he can shield-dash (E) into a free W (Path Maker) knockback-stun combo. Back off and reset the wave instead of contesting.

yourWindow.what: This is your all-in window. Open with Q (Broken Wings) to close, land W (Ki Burst) for the stun, and dump autos — without E he has no shield and no dash to disengage, so the fight is yours to finish.

start.why: Measured as the dominant start on this patch (45% WR, 90.9% pick) — the extra sustain matters since you're playing a defensive matchup and will take short trades, not long ones.

boots.why: 61.5% WR and the leading pick (61.9%) — the ability haste shortens your W (Ki Burst) and E (Valor) cooldowns, which is exactly the resource you're starved for against his faster-scaling kit.

core.why: Highest-performing core path measured (100% WR in its sample) — the shield proc covers you through his Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke while you commit to an all-in.
Stacks armor shred to cut through his bonus resistances, which otherwise make your all-in windows close too slowly.
Converts his burst (W knockback-stun combo, R All Out) into delayed damage so you survive to finish your own combo.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is a stat-check matchup once E (Footwork) is down — Conqueror's adaptive force and healing let you win the extended trade instead of just the opening burst.

summoners.why: The clear majority pick on this patch (90.5% pick rate, 42.1% WR) — Ignite punishes his E (Footwork) shield once it's burned through, since he has no way to heal it back mid-fight.

playing.title: Never all-in into E (Footwork) up
playing.detail: If he still has his shield-dash available, your Q+W combo just feeds him a free reset. Wait for it to go on cooldown (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s) before committing.

playing.title: Respect 2-stack Q range
playing.detail: Once he has 2 Ntofo Strikes stacks, his next hit fires a shockwave that pulls you in. Don't poke into range when you see his stack counter at 2.

playing.title: Use E (Valor) to block his opener
playing.detail: Valor lets you step forward while blocking incoming damage — eat his Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke with it before you commit your own combo, not after.

playing.title: Hold R (Blade of Exile) until his R is down
playing.detail: His R (All Out) knocks you through walls into a transformed, harder-hitting version of himself on a 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown. Don't commit your ultimate into a fight he can flip with his.

playing.title: Track your own Runic Blade charges
playing.detail: Your passive only pays off on autos that spend charges — land Q or W first so your follow-up auto actually hits for the bonus instead of wasting the window.

playing.title: Freeze the wave when behind
playing.detail: Since he holds lane and solo-kill advantage, deny him easy Q (Ntofo Strikes) pokes by holding the wave near your tower rather than trading freely.

playing.title: Watch his passive mark before trading
playing.detail: If one of his abilities has already marked you, his next auto deals bonus damage — disengage or block it with E (Valor) rather than trading through it.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the tactical reasoning — cooldown windows, stack tells, trade timing — is my own read on the mechanics, not measured data.
